name: Pembrolizumab
summary: A humanised IgG4 monoclonal antibody against PD-1, an off switch on T cells. Blocking PD-1 stops tumour cells from using PD-L1 and PD-L2 to switch T cells off.

target.name: PD-1 receptor on T cells
target.cell: T cell facing a tumour cell

journey.title: Infused into a vein
journey.text: Pembrolizumab is given as an intravenous infusion, so it enters the bloodstream directly, with no absorption step.

journey.title: Circulates for weeks
journey.text: Like other IgG antibodies it is rescued from breakdown by the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), which helps give it a terminal half-life of about 22 days.

journey.title: Meets T cells in lymph nodes
journey.text: PD-1 is found on activated T cells. Blocking it can act on T cells in lymph nodes as well as in the tumour.

journey.title: Reaches the tumour
journey.text: In the tumour, tumour cells and some immune cells can display PD-L1, which switches T cells off through PD-1.

journey.title: Broken down like other proteins
journey.text: Antibodies are cleared mainly by protein catabolism inside cells throughout the body, not by liver CYP enzymes or kidney filtration of the intact molecule.

mechanism.title: The brake is on
mechanism.text: PD-L1 or PD-L2 on the tumour cell engages PD-1 on the T cell and damps down its activity.

mechanism.title: Pembrolizumab binds PD-1
mechanism.text: The antibody binds PD-1 and blocks its interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2.

mechanism.title: The brake is released
mechanism.text: Releasing PD-1 pathway inhibition restores T-cell activity, including the anti-tumour response.

mechanism.title: T cells attack the tumour
mechanism.text: Reactivated T cells can recognise and kill tumour cells. The same release of brakes on T cells in healthy tissue causes immune-mediated side effects.

facts.label: Target
facts.value: PD-1; blocks binding of PD-L1 and PD-L2

simplified: The tumour–T-cell contact is drawn as one flat interface. Real immune synapses are 3D and hold many other receptor pairs.
T-cell activation also needs the T-cell receptor to recognise antigen on MHC; the figure shows only the PD-1 brake.
The body map is a schematic, and the tumour position is illustrative only.
